account: RL-Math's weight change is small (about 0.1-0.3 % of each matrix's norm) and low-rank in effect: the top 8 singular directions of each matrix's change (about 10 % of its squared norm), added to the base at 1.5x, match RL's hard328 vote (216.25 vs 215.92 of 328) and 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain on problems the cued base never solves, while a random rank-8 edit of the same size does nothing.

The outcome reward does not make those directions: an LM-judge RL run concentrates its change just as much (top-8 share 0.127 vs 0.135), Think-SFT's imitation change reads the same inputs (4.8x chance), and Code-RL's change lies in them 5x more than Think-SFT's, so on-policy RL on step-by-step text strengthens a deliberative mode the base already runs, one mode shared by Math and Code.

Each sample gets two changes: a switch into a deliberative opening, which RL puts into the weights early (at step 100 the cue adds only 8.5 of 500 and cap hits equal the cued base's) and which a partial edit applies all-or-none per sample (Code 1x: deliberative answers right at the cued rate, others near the plain rate); and a lower per-step slip rate plus a re-ranking of routes toward RL's, which grows later and lengthens right answers from 1.15x the cued base's at step 100 to 1.6x at the end.

Inference reproduces the switch fully: a three-token cue, or a hand-written three-key edit of one tensor (397 vs 410 of 500 for the cue), switches the base, and T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 removes the repetition loops that fill 52-63 % of T 0.6 attempts past 4,096 tokens, so the base goes from 45 to 82 against RL's 93 on MATH-500.

Inference reproduces the slip cut only in part: the base's wrong answers mostly scatter (same-problem pair agreement 0.26), so a vote over 4 removes 7-8 points of one-off slips, but no vote can create a right answer the base never samples, so RL keeps 8.8 points on hard328 (224 vs 195 of 328) and the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins.

Code splits the same way, with Code-RL's own directions: the Code edit's fixes are mostly problems the base passes in other samples (0.75), and its pass rate rises 7 points over a random edit against 1.5 for Math's directions, so the switch is shared across rewards while the slip cut belongs to the reward's own domain.

consequences.claim: Code-RL 3.1's change falls into RL-Math 3.1's top-8 singular pairs (left and right together) about 11x more than into RL-Zero-General's pairs, because Math and Code RL strengthen the same step-by-step deliberation mode and an LM-judge chat reward does not use it (S2, S6). An RL run that merely starts from the same base would give a ratio near 1.
consequences.why_new: F51 and result-105d5c use cap_right with Code over Think-SFT, and result-9d979a uses subspace overlaps; no fact or result uses the joint (cap_both) capture of one RL change in another reward's pairs, or Math pairs against General pairs.
consequences.statistic: median over matrices of cap_both(code31>math31) / cap_both(code31>general30), a dimensionless ratio
consequences.rows: all test matrices (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down, every layer) in cap.jsonl
consequences.computation: 1) For each test matrix, read cap['code31>math31']['cap_both'] and cap['code31>general30']['cap_both']. 2) Take their ratio per matrix. 3) Statistic = median of the ratios over matrices. 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of matrices with replacement, median each time, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: Any RL run's top-8 pairs from the same base capture Code-RL's change equally (shared optimizer and base structure), so the ratio is about 1. Explore checks: Think-SFT's change in the same two pair sets gives 2.57; Code in IF/General gives 0.36; norm ratio Math/General 2.07; top-8 share ratio 0.99.

consequences.claim: What RL-Math and Code-RL changes have in common sits in Math's top-8 singular block: the full-matrix cosine of the two changes is about as large as the top-8 block alone can carry, R = cos / sqrt(cap_both(code31>math31) x top8_share(math31)) near 1.2, because the shared deliberation mode is carried by the few strengthened directions (S1, S2). A shared component spread across directions would need R near 26.
consequences.why_new: No fact or result relates the full-delta cosine (anatomy pair cos) to the top-8 block capture; the board shows overlaps and cap ratios only separately.
consequences.statistic: median over matrices of R = cos(rl_math, rl_code) / sqrt(cap_both(code31>math31) * top8_share(rl_math)), dimensionless
consequences.rows: all test matrices present in both anatomy.jsonl and cap.jsonl (all 112)
consequences.computation: 1) For each test matrix, take c = anatomy pair['rl_math-rl_code']['cos'], s = anatomy delta['rl_math']['top8_share'], b = cap['code31>math31']['cap_both']. 2) R = c / sqrt(b * s). 3) Statistic = median of R over matrices. 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of matrices, median each time, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: The shared component is diffuse, i.e. it falls into Math's top-8 block only at chance (64/(d_out*d_in)): R_null = c / sqrt(64/(d_out*d_in) * s), median 25.98 [23.30, 28.07] on explore; using the base matrix's own top-8 block instead of Math's gives 7.34 [6.33, 8.30]; Think-SFT's version of R gives 0.09.

consequences.claim: Across matrices, the pattern of where RL-Math 3.1 concentrates its change (top-8 share, each module family's median removed) follows Code-RL 3.1's pattern much more than RL-Zero-General's: D = rho(Math31, Code31) - rho(Math31, General30) about 0.47, because Math and Code strengthen the same deliberation mode in the same matrices (S2).
consequences.why_new: F24 compares Math with IF and Think-SFT, F62 compares Code with Think-SFT and IF; no fact or result compares Math with Code against General.
consequences.statistic: Spearman rho(Math31, Code31) minus Spearman rho(Math31, General30) of family-median-removed per-matrix top-8 shares, a difference of correlations
consequences.computation: 1) For each key in (math31, code31, general30): per module family (q,k,v,o,gate,up,down), subtract the family median of top8_share[key] over the matrices in the sample. 2) Spearman rank correlation of residuals Math31 vs Code31, and Math31 vs General30, over matrices. 3) D = difference. 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of matrices, recompute medians and correlations each time, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: Every RL run concentrates in the same matrices through shared base structure and module, so D is 0. The size-only alternative (the same D on per-matrix relative norm, norm/base norm) gives 0.066 [-0.049, 0.155] on explore.

weights_cell.statistic: median over matrices of the cosine between the rank-8 truncations of the two changes, cos(T8(RL-Math 3.1 - base), T8(Code-RL 3.1 - base)), dimensionless
weights_cell.matrices: all 224 (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down of 32 layers)
weights_cell.computation: 1) Per matrix, dm = W_math31 - W_base and dc = W_code31 - W_base in float32. 2) Per delta, SVD; T8 = sum of the top 8 singular triplets sigma_i u_i v_i^T. 3) cos = <T8(dm), T8(dc)>_F / (||T8(dm)||_F ||T8(dc)||_F). 4) Median over the 224 matrices.
weights_cell.why: S1-S2 put the shared Math/Code mode in the few strengthened directions, so most of the full-delta cosine (median 0.012) lies in the top-8 parts, whose share of the norm is about 0.10 each: 0.012/sqrt(0.10*0.106) is about 0.12, minus the part outside the block (R about 1.2), giving about 0.10. A blind alternative (shared component diffuse, or size/chance alone) predicts the truncations are no more aligned than the whole deltas, about 0.012, and chance gives about 0.002.
